question: Must this provider-native acknowledgement and Signal transaction change include compatible-client fault-injection proof before the draft is accepted, or are the focused tests sufficient for this protocol surface?
rationale: Repository policy explicitly asks for authoritative provider verification and, when practical, an actual client; the patch changes ordering that can affect both delivery and cryptographic session state, which unit tests and a green verify check cannot fully settle.

options.title: Require compatible-client proof
options.body: Keep the draft open until a redacted live run or runtime transcript demonstrates recorder failure, retry, durable acceptance, acknowledgement, and session continuity.

options.title: Accept focused test proof
options.body: Allow the focused fault-injection suite to satisfy fidelity review if maintainers judge a real-client failure setup impractical and manually validate the modeled ordering.

recommendation.title: Require compatible-client proof
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open until a redacted live run or runtime transcript demonstrates recorder failure, retry, durable acceptance, acknowledgement, and session continuity.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed repository member connected to the current WhatsApp transaction design in the supplied history.
